title: docs(skills): objectstack-api and objectstack-i18n teach the request-locale userMessage
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DCMMD2o5CacLGZAtxYhix4a)_

Fixes #32844

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** API 技能文档「Error Envelopes」一节和 i18n 技能文档各加一段，写明接口返回给用户看的 `userMessage` 用请求的语言：平台自己写的文字按「请求语言 → 工作区默认语言 → `en`」逐级回退，应用自己写的拒绝文字走应用自己的翻译。同时写明保存/发布时的建议列表和 422 问题列表，每条也可能带 `userMessage`。
- **为什么改：** #32790 已把这条规则写进契约，技能文档还没教。AI 照旧文档写客户端时，会把给开发者看的英文 `message` 直接显示给用户，或者自己再维护一张翻译表。
- **风险与回滚：** 只改两份技能文档，不改代码和协议；回滚就是 revert 本 PR。新增文字用同一文件里删掉的重复内容付清，两份文档的 token 数都比原来少（API 5157 降到 5152，i18n 5921 降到 5918），没有抬任何上限。
- **先看：** `skills/objectstack-api/SKILL.md`「Error Envelopes」里新增的一段；`skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md` 新增的「Server-Composed User Text」一节；API 文档「Auth Configuration」里删掉的限流示例代码块（上文 D6 一节有同样三个键的示例）。
- **两分钟验证：** `node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs | grep -E "objectstack-(api|i18n)/SKILL"`，预期读到 5152 和 5918 两行，都带 ✓。
- **需要你做的：** 审阅并批准本 PR（`skills/**` 是受管面，Tier H）。

## What changes

- **`skills/objectstack-api/SKILL.md`, § Error Envelopes & the Code Ledger.** One paragraph is added after the ledger paragraphs. It states, in the wording of the Language section of `ApiErrorSchema.userMessage` (`packages/spec/src/api/contract.zod.ts`): the text is in the request's locale and a consumer renders it as received and keeps no per-code translation table; platform-composed text follows one ladder over the platform locale table (`PLATFORM_LOCALES`, `@objectstack/spec/system`), the locale the request names (its `Accept-Language`, or `?locale` on the REST door), else the workspace default, else `en`, each code read whole and then one subtag shorter at a time; app-authored text, such as a hook's catalogued refusal, is not on this ladder and has no `en` floor. The paragraph closes with the finding twin: the save / publish doors' `advisories[]` and the 422 `issues[]` share one element, `RuntimeAuthoringIssueSchema` (`api/protocol.zod.ts`), which carries an optional `userMessage` beside the stable `rule`, while `message` / `hint` stay developer-facing English.
- **`skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md`, new section "Server-Composed User Text (`userMessage`)"**, placed before "Translation Workflow Best Practices". Two bullets: the platform-composed ladder (with the contract's `fr-FR` and `zh-Hant-US` examples and its sentence that a Traditional Chinese code is never handed Simplified text), and app-authored refusal text, served through the hook-refusal translation key (`hooks.HOOK.refusals.CODE.message`, spelled in the skill with its two placeholders) in the caller's locale, negotiated over the locales the app's translations hold, otherwise as declared, with no `en` floor.
- **Payment, `objectstack-api`** (same-file restatements): the two auto-generated rows and the carve-out row of the Endpoint Naming table (the route listing and "The path carve-out" teach them); the lead-in of Authentication & Authorization (the Skill Boundaries table sends permissions to objectstack-data); the `RateLimitConfigSchema` example block in Auth Configuration and the parenthesis before it (the D6 section shows the same three keys and names the schema); the `authRequired` comment in the endpoint example (the D6 section says omission is safe); the lead-in line of Realtime Subscriptions; the tail of Best Practice 2. The D6 section now names the entry `RateLimitConfigSchema` is imported from (`@objectstack/spec/shared`), which the removed block was the only place to show.
- **Payment, `objectstack-i18n`** (same-file restatements): the BCP-47 callout (Naming Conventions has the row); the "mirrors the shipped `examples/app-todo`" sentence (Shipped examples says it); the "Critical" callout under the naming table; the `i18n.t` usage block (Service Contract documents `t`); the second ICU sentence; the tail of the `loadTranslations` bullet (step 4 says it); the "Run the workflow as written" sentence; the body of step 3 (now a pointer to Translation Coverage); two asides in the retired-shape pitfall; the "Ignoring Coverage Reports" pitfall; and the `os lint --i18n-strict` sentence in Verify your work (Translation Coverage says it).
- **`.changeset/32844-skills-request-locale-user-message.md`:** `@objectstack/skills` patch.

## Why

PR #32790 (card #32655) merged on 2026-11-12. The contract now says that `userMessage` is in the request's locale and declares the ladder for platform-composed text, and `RuntimeAuthoringIssueSchema` gained an optional `userMessage`. Neither skill said so. `objectstack-api` named `userMessage` once, as the first thing a flow-failure renderer reads, with no language rule; `objectstack-i18n` did not name it. An agent writing a client from the skills would show the developer-facing English `message`, or keep its own translation table per code.

## Tests

- No test file changes: the diff is prose. No ablation, for the same reason.
- Evals read against the edited files. `skills/objectstack-api/evals/endpoints-auth-routes.json` (7 cases) and `skills/objectstack-i18n/evals/bundles-locales-coverage.json` (10 cases): no case grades an error envelope or `userMessage`, and every `must_contain` token is still taught. Case 2 of the API eval asks for `authRequired`, `rateLimit`, `enabled: true` and `maxRequests`; all four remain in the D6 section after the Auth Configuration block is removed. No eval edit.

## Acceptance notes

- **Branch name.** The platform pins this card thread to `claude/project-thread-2rxbd0`; the claim (6838566930) names it.
- **Wording.** The added text follows the contract's sentences. Two things the contract's Language section says are left out as producer-side detail a skill reader does not author against: the `ExecutionContext.locale` fold and the `renderOperationMessage` single-locale note.
- **One removed block was a checked example.** The `RateLimitConfigSchema` block carried the `os:check` marker. `check:skill-examples` still passes, and the import path it showed moved into the D6 section.
- **No eval added.** The card asks that the existing evals still pass, not for a new case.
